name: Mohammad Reza I of Iran
summary: A modernising monarch who ruled Iran for 38 years, pursuing top-down reform through the White Revolution (land reform, women's suffrage, profit sharing, literacy and health corps) funded by oil revenue, with a large military and alignment with the West. He held that a constitutional monarchy was the only workable form of rule for Iran, banned the Tudeh party, replaced the two tolerated parties with a single party in 1975 and relied on SAVAK against opposition, while opposing clerical rule and Soviet influence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Set out five minimum entitlements for every citizen including medical care, with the state or charities stepping in, and later created nationwide social security, free infant nutrition and rural Health Corps clinics.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Labour legislation under the White Revolution tied the minimum wage for unskilled labour to the cost of living, so it rose with prices.

public-ownership.rationale: Kept railways, telephones, munitions, steel and oil state-run, yet sold state factory shares to the public and workers and favoured private enterprise in most other fields.

unions-good.rationale: Wrote that he firmly believes in free trade unions as an instrument of democracy, necessary so economic democracy reaches industry.

property-fundamental.rationale: Limited private ownership of arable land by law, nationalised forests and water, and broke up large estates, paying compensation in state-factory shares rather than treating ownership as untouchable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Said government should regulate industry and commerce in the public interest, fixed maximum prices, fined and jailed profiteers, and forced private firms to sell 49 percent of shares to workers.

cut-welfare.rationale: Rejected the argument that the needy are poor through laziness and expanded pensions, social security and free food for mothers and infants.

worker-ownership.rationale: The Thirteenth Principle of the White Revolution (1975) required private firms over five years old to sell 49 percent of their shares to their workers; he said workers should become co-owners.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Defended SAVAK as an intelligence service comparable to the KGB, CIA or FBI needed against subversion and terrorism.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Halted poppy cultivation by stern measures and set up treatment centres for addicts.

strong-leader.rationale: Told Fallaci he is authoritarian because reforming a largely illiterate country requires it, and stressed unity imposed from above by the sovereign.

empower-police-military.rationale: Built Iran's armed forces into a leading regional power on the argument that strict independence made military strength a necessity.

decide-locally.rationale: Favoured provincial and municipal autonomy, village equity houses and elected councils, while keeping the army, finance, police and public education centralised.

rehabilitation.rationale: Described prison reform schools and a Karaj centre rehabilitating beggars as part of social policy.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Revived Persian poetry, music, folklore and historical teaching and said Iran must stay faithful to its ancestral tradition.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Backed the UN wholeheartedly, called for a future world authority to keep peace, and wanted world economic institutions strengthened.

nation-first.rationale: Wrote that his foreign policy served only one country, Iran, and told Fallaci friendship with the US did not make Iran a slave of the US.

limit-growth.rationale: Held up ever greater material prosperity as a goal and ran a rapid growth programme, though he also replanted forests and set conservation policy.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Planned and began building nuclear power plants, with a target of 25,000 MW of nuclear electricity and a research centre.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Described comprehensive planning in which government credit and technical help were channelled to needed industries (he declined to finance a silk plant in favour of sugar), run through the Plan Organization.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Said economic democracy means many independent entrepreneurs and farmers, and distributed land to small peasant owners while rejecting collectivised farming.

one-party-rule.rationale: Founded the single Resurgence (Rastakhiz) party in 1975 but wrote in 1980 that creating it was an error and that Sadat was right to return to pluralism; in 1961 he rejected the one-party state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Said monarchy is the only possible way of governing Iran and that it has served the country for 2,500 years.

democracy-best.rationale: In 1961 called democracy the system that secures freedom, but by 1973-80 rejected Western-style democracy and 'authentic parliamentary democracy' as a caricature.

right-to-secede.rationale: Sent troops to crush the Soviet-backed autonomous Azerbaijan and Kurdish republics and stressed that the crown unites Iran's ethnic groups.

separate-church-state.rationale: Praised his father's compromise confining clergy to religious matters, yet kept Shia Islam as state religion, called himself Defender of the Faith and funded mosques and seminaries.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Asked whether anyone worthy of the name could flog, stone or amputate on the pretext that caliphs of the Middle Ages did so, and ran Iran on modern codes.

military-superiority.rationale: Built armed forces he said would be among the finest in the world and told Fallaci Iran was strong enough to resist a major war.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Described Iran as an empire of diverse ethnic groups with different languages, held together by the crown.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said everyone is entitled to a decent minimum but that anyone who earns more by honest means is welcome to it; also wrote that redistribution is not the answer, creating new wealth is.

limit-population.rationale: Cited government-backed organisations teaching infant care and family planning and noted the strain of a million new mouths a year.

collective-farming.rationale: Said Iran wanted none of the Chinese 'ant-hill' collectivised society and favoured independent farmers, though later farm corporations let farmers swap land for shares.

conscription.rationale: Staffed the Literacy, Health and Development Corps with conscripts and kept a conscript army.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said Iran harboured no expansionist notions, though he sent troops to Oman and occupied the Tunbs and Abu Musa in 1971.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Iran kept a de facto Israeli trade mission and cooperated with Israel, but he also opposed Israeli annexation of territory and later criticised Palestinian pressure.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Gave workers shares and profit bonuses but criticised post-revolution bodies of rank-and-file workers who dismissed directors and set production and pay.

class-collaboration.rationale: Said profit sharing and employee share ownership would cement the union between owners, technicians and workers and encouraged close labour-management cooperation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Helped expand libraries, restore ancient art and traditions and protect old village quarters.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Opposed legal inferiority of women and backed equal opportunity, but told Mission readers that literal equality of men and women is a confusion and told Fallaci women are not equal to men in ability.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Built up the National Iranian Oil Company, raised output to five or six million barrels a day to fund development, and built refineries and gas industries.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Wrote that although one inherits a crown power must be earned with the people's help and used only on their behalf.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Outlawed the Tudeh party after the 1949 attempt on his life as a threat to the regime and the country's territorial integrity.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Made his five principles of social justice a minimum for every person and said he could not stand privileged people growing rich while others were in dire want.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Imposed martial law and a military government in 1978 and used special tribunals without appeal for price-control offences.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Government fixed maximum retail prices for bread and meat in Tehran, subsidised five staple foods and ran fixed-price stores for workers; the 1975 anti-profiteering campaign set price guidelines enforced by special tribunals.

head-commands-forces.rationale: As king he was Commander-in-Chief, declared war and made peace, and appointed the prime minister and ministers.

clerical-rule.rationale: Condemned Khomeini's clerical regime as a theocracy and reign of terror and described the 'Black' clergy as reactionary opponents of reform.

death-penalty.rationale: Said death is normal for proved traitors, let treason trials end in executions (Fatemi), and told Fallaci it is right and necessary to shoot certain people; he also pardoned assassins.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Said the White Revolution needed a permanent state of urgency and that letting saboteurs act freely would have prevented it, calling Western-style democracy premature for Iran.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Proposed in 1973 an International Fund for Aid financed by industrial countries and OPEC members, and urged a new deal for developing countries.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Wrote in 1980 of his repeated firm intention to avoid even the possession of nuclear weapons; earlier remarks that Iran might acquire them are on record.

collective-defense.rationale: Backed NATO, CENTO and the US bilateral pact as co-operative international security and cited the defensive purpose of the Baghdad Pact.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Told Fallaci Iran could not accept a country, in this case Israel, annexing territory through the use of arms.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Endorsed his father's removal of judicial and educational functions from the clergy, kept clergy to religious matters and pressed land reform against clerical opposition.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Wrote in 1961 that under a party system the Shah must serve as a focal point of unity above lesser interests, though he later led his own single party.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Ordered his troops into Azerbaijan to put down its separatist rebellion once and for all in 1946.

land-redistribution.rationale: Distributed Crown lands and enacted the 1962-63 land reform, the first White Revolution principle, which limited landlords' holdings and sold land to peasants who worked it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Said women were free to wear or not wear the chador in his reign and that those who wish to veil may, but denounced forcing women into the veil.

elective-rulers.rationale: Told Fallaci monarchy is the only possible way of governing Iran, preferable to anarchy, oligarchy or dictatorship, and said Iranian democracy can flourish only under a constitutional monarchy.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Said he reigns but does not rule, yet also said he was the first Shah to use his constitutional powers fully, held a signature and veto and dissolved parliament.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Told deputies he could not tolerate privileged people growing rich and sleek while others were in want, and criticised self-centred citizens who acquiesced in poverty.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Said he was not preaching a rigid pattern of democracy and told Fallaci he did not want Western-style democracy for Iran.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Signed a 1955 law to attract and protect foreign private capital with guaranteed profit withdrawal and just compensation, and an investment-guarantee deal with the US.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Described the National Assembly as having sole authority over budgetary and tax bills.

single-official-language.rationale: Cited teaching Persian across the country, under central control of public education, as a common bond for a mosaic of nationalities.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: From 1972 Iran, with US backing, supplied Iraqi Kurdish fighters against Baghdad until the 1975 Algiers Accord.

job-guarantee.rationale: Labour principles declared that every Iranian has a right to employment, with unemployment pay until employment offices placed a jobless worker.

religious-nation.rationale: Stressed that Iran is an assemblage of peoples of different ethnic character, language and religious belief and praised minority representation in parliament.

defeat-communism.rationale: Called Communist subversion the main danger and doubted that coexistence would avert war, yet kept neighbourly trade and border agreements with the USSR.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Outlawed the Tudeh party, banned the existing parties in 1975 for the single Rastakhiz party and said anyone who disliked the system could take a passport and leave.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Joined the Baghdad Pact/CENTO and a bilateral US security agreement, writing that neutrality had failed Persia in two world wars.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Explained the constitution passes the crown to a male heir in direct line and divorced Soraya because the nation required an heir.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Wrote that true faith follows the spirit of a religion, not sectarian dogmatism, and that the Koran's truths are served by emancipating women, not by medieval punishments.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Stressed that Persian monarchy and culture run unbroken for about 2,500 years since Cyrus, and celebrated that at Persepolis.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Nationalised Iran's surface and underground water in 1968 as belonging to everyone, and built public water systems, clinics and hospitals, while leaving other services to private providers.

second-chamber.rationale: Brought the constitutionally provided Senate into being in his reign, half appointed by him, and defended a two-house parliament.

family-wage.rationale: Held that a man's income should be sufficient for him to secure food, clothing, housing, medical care and education for himself and his family.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Said the revolution had to rest on spiritual principles and religious belief and that youth needed solid spiritual and moral training alongside technical knowledge.

communal-electorates.rationale: Pointed with pride to the reserved deputies for Jews, Zoroastrians, Assyrians and Armenians in the National Assembly.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Wrote that the Soviets set up puppet Kurdish and Azerbaijani regimes in 1945-46 and said the British fostered Kurdish separatism.

free-public-college.rationale: Instituted free education for the first eight years and free further study for students who agreed to government service, plus scholarships.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Profit-sharing law required employers to conclude collective agreements with workers, while the state itself set minimum wages by law.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Argued for a just, periodically revised oil price and international cooperation and said a new deal must be struck with the underdeveloped countries.

farm-price-support.rationale: Agricultural and Development Bank loans, rural cooperatives and cheap state grain supplies were set up to secure small farmers.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: from his statements that women may manage their own fortunes and deserve complete equality with men in all fields; he never discussed land inheritance.

women-suffrage.rationale: The fifth White Revolution principle gave women the vote and the right to hold office; he argued women should not be classed with the insane and criminals.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Accepted self-determination for Bahrain in 1971, where only a sixth of the population was Iranian, and Bahrain opted for independence.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Hoped Persia could merge antiquity and modernity and called the Great Civilization faithful to ancestral tradition while using the best of other civilizations.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Criticised denying women the right to divorce that husbands hold and said Islam is served by giving women complete equality.

national-resource-control.rationale: Called himself an ardent supporter of the 1951 oil nationalisation and said he wrested Iran's oil resources from foreign ownership; the 1973 agreement gave the state company control of the fields.

notes: Views changed on party politics: in 1961 he rejected the one-party state and promoted a two-party system; he founded the single Rastakhiz party in 1975; in 1980 he called that an error, which is the answer used. On democracy he moved from praising it (1961) to rejecting Western-style democracy (1973-80). His 1974 remarks about possibly acquiring nuclear weapons conflict with his 1980 statement that he intended to avoid them; the 1980 position is used. The White Revolution (1967), Toward the Great Civilization (1977), the Mike Wallace (1976) and David Frost (1980) interviews could not be retrieved as texts; the Fallaci interview was read only through a page summary. His statements about SAVAK were self-defence and are not treated as evidence that no torture occurred; answers on surveillance and suppressing opposition rest on the record of banned parties and SAVAK's creation. Treatment of the 1953 coup, Persepolis 1971 and the Israel relationship rests on reference summaries, so answers there are low confidence or null.
